correctness.rationale: All domain and normalization factors were reconstructed from Guillot (2010) Eq.27. The identity \(4(T_s^4)'=B+s(Q-P)\), the strictly decreasing ratio \(P/(B/s+Q)\), and the monotonicity of \(f=P-Q\) on \(\{f>0\}\) establish exactly one strict global minimum iff \(s(P(0)-Q(0))>B\). The transverse \(P=Q\) crossing gives the finite-depth \(s^{-1}\) correction; the least high exponent gives the \(\log s\) law in the absence of low bands. The exact two-band scaling follows by substitution around the limiting \(P=Q\) depth; endpoint asymptotics follow by Taylor and dominant exponent. Boundary s=s_c, absent high or low bands, and equality-opacity neutral bands are explicitly treated. Packaged check.py, run in this execution, completed 5000 derivative, 3000 shape, and 1000 crossover tests, which are supplementary rather than universal proofs.

value.rationale: A sharp, parameterized response of planetary temperature inversion depth to irradiation is a motivated missing diagnostic in the widely used analytic grey-atmosphere approximation. Deep-penetrating stellar spectral fractions distinguish finite saturation from indefinite logarithmic deepening; the exact two-band scaling quantifies the singular crossover for a weak transparent band. The classification is natural for spectral radiative transfer, not a hand-picked dimensionless invariant. No empirical or multi-opacity physical claim is inferred.
